story_structure.value: Declarative contrast — the delivered build's declared architecture (its script doc): the fork is stated in the first line ('Two futures share one name: AGI'), ARTIFICIAL is defined (L2), the second future surfaces (L3), the system is claimed as parts (L4: 'the same six parts, every time'), the inventory is spoken (L5–L10: the LLM; the HARNESS; INSTRUCTIONS; HOOKS; FILES; TOOLS), the system is worn (L11: 'a digital CORTEX, around your own mind'), invariance is asserted (L12–L13: nothing added or taken away; only one thing changes), the ownership question lands (L14), the fork resolves (L15–L16: apart/someone else's vs worn/yours), and the triple close seals it (L17–L19: 'Same letters. / Same parts. / One of them is YOURS.'). The doc's doctrine map is the structure's reasoning: two parts as the only count, the LLM a utility working inside the harness, the harness organic — a living file system — its interior contents, not parts.
story_structure.rationale: Structure is decided in the delivered build's own script doc — its Architecture paragraph and Doctrine map — the only place it could be: the board logs this piece's Narrative Gate item 'na' (its checklist predates the gate's application here). Two honesty notes ride with the field. (1) The doc's narration table is the doc's own 18-line iteration; the delivered regrouping speaks 19 lines (see transcript.md). (2) The doc's change log records the doctrine restructure REPLACING the six-parts framing ('there is no six-count left to signal'), yet the delivered L4 still speaks 'the same six parts' and the inventory that follows is six named items — the delivered text is a hybrid the doc does not describe, carried openly in transcript_line_divergence. The tokens iteration's own declared structure — one stage, the scale machine, 17 verbatim-prose beats (its script doc's visual-beats table; audit structure entries EL-12…EL-16) — is the same opening's earlier form, recorded in the decisions layer.

The reconciliation states the headline form: script 17 lines/237 words, delivered 19 lines/131 words — 'the script does not govern the build (recorded)'. Which text a future rebuild would lock — and whether the piece's two published iterations (the tokens render stands at 84.50 s under the same board title) are one piece developing or two pieces sharing an id — is a rebuild-time decision the records deliberately leave open; the kit's ruling stands in the meantime: 'reconcile wording only at a rebuild.'
